issues.description: The header declares the class with a different name than its constructors/implementation: example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp declares 'class Image24' while the constructors and implementation use 'Bitmap24'. This mismatch prevents the constructors (Bitmap24::Bitmap24) declared/defined in the .cpp from matching any class declaration in the header, causing immediate compilation errors and confusion about the intended class name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the header and implementation consistent by renaming the class in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from 'Image24' to 'Bitmap24' (so the class name matches the constructors and the .cpp). Alternatively, rename the constructors/implementation to match 'Image24'. Prefer the first option to match the file name and the solution repository. Ensure the include guard and any references use the corrected class name.

issues.description: The header in the TEMPLATE_REPOSITORY declares the class as 'Image24' (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) while the implementation (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) and the SOLUTION_REPOSITORY header use the class name 'Bitmap24'. This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual entity (the bitmap image class) will prevent compilation and forces students to resolve an unnecessary naming mismatch instead of focusing on the exercise. It is an unintended inconsistency between template and solution and conflicts with the problem statement requirement that the assignment must compile.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template header from 'Image24' to 'Bitmap24' (and ensure include guards and constructor/destructor declarations match) so the header and implementation use the same identifier. This aligns the template with the solution and satisfies the 'must compile' requirement.
